analysis.title: GS Johnstone - GS TMT SPEC SALES: AI/semis bounce; ASM raises; Adyen margin debate; DSY mixed; Temenos EBIT beat; KPN solid, Telenor mixed 28 Oct 2026
key_insights: Overnight earnings steadied the AI trade. Celestica rose 12% and SK Hynix gained 10.5% after a Q3 beat and a shareholder return plan, which lifted Samsung 8% ahead of its October 29 results. Attention turns to Alphabet and Microsoft tonight and Amazon tomorrow.

The desk sees tentative renewed buying across AI, helped by better earnings, oversold conditions and easing selling pressure. After about three months of weak performance, investors may want steadier prices and fewer open risks before adding materially, so choppy trading remains the base case.

Adyen delivered 20% organic growth (about 200bps of the total was inorganic) and reiterated FY net revenue growth of 21-23% y/y at constant currency. The new margin message is the debate: it now expects about 50% margins for 2026 versus Street 52%, and it withdrew the medium-term margin target of above 55% by FY28.

Adyen management ties the margin reset to investment in people (senior staff in San Francisco) and to scaling recent acquisitions more aggressively. The open question is whether the Street raises revenue and trims margins, or only trims margins and waits for the topline.

Dassault Systemes (DSY) headlines look better than the underlying results. The Q3 beat came from licences, recurring revenue missed, ARR has not accelerated, and the raised FY guidance largely reflects the ArisGlobal acquisition. Next catalyst is the CMD on 17 November.

ASM International delivered a beat and raise with a 2027 revenue guide of more than €5.7bn at constant currency, 5% above consensus. Advanced logic and foundry (2nm and 1.4nm) are expected to be the strongest growth driver in 2027, with strong memory growth also expected. It is the first beat in this space to be rewarded.

NXP fell about 8% after hours on in-line results and mixed Q4 guidance that fell short of bullish expectations. GS reads this as modestly negative for analog peers with auto exposure (ADI, ON, and IFX and STM in Europe). The desk still thinks many investors want to buy IFX after its guide, and the STM debate is the 2027 gross margin.

Post-print reactions show how high the bar is. Seagate fell about 7% after hours despite a beat and guidance above consensus, Teradyne fell 6% after hours as its EPS beat shrank to about 10% from 20-30%, and Logitech fell 7% despite a beat and better guide because margins could have been better.

SK Hynix reported revenue of 104tr won (+328% y/y) and operating profit of 88tr won, both above consensus. It has long-term agreements with 14 major customers covering more than 50% of 2027 and 2028 capacity and expects memory demand to outpace supply through 2030.

Temenos again missed on revenue (subscriptions 6% below expectations, blamed on a delayed large African deal) but beat on cost-driven EBIT. FY26 EBIT growth guidance was raised to about 12% and reported EPS growth guidance to about 10%. Hitting the Q4 subscription and SaaS guide needs 16% growth, and reliance on large deals adds quarterly volatility.

KPN's Q3 was in line with FY guidance reiterated and the stock is expected to trade flat. Telenor's Q3 was mixed with FY guidance reiterated. Its group EBITDA beat came from opex savings pulled forward from Q4 and its working capital beat from a Grameenphone VAT timing benefit that reverses in Q4. Telenor will run its buyback over 2 years instead of 3 at the same total amount.

Orange's call was solid: French consolidation timetable unchanged (signing by end-2026, closing by end-2027, long-stop date 6 December), Spain improving, and no automatic pricing pressure seen from agentic AI or satellite. GS says Street estimates need to go up.

American Tower's call centred on Starlink as a potential scale new tower customer. Management would not discuss talks but said its sites, quality and speed to get on air make it the first call for any large network builder.

US trading: NDX posted back-to-back 1%+ gains for the first time in about 3 months, but breadth was narrow with about 60% of S&P names lower. The desk's flow read is that supply abatement drives most of the bounce, with early but limited evidence of more offense across the AI complex after near-zero offense in recent weeks.

Visa reported a roughly in-line quarter with in-line FY2027 guidance. GS sees it as a clearing event that keeps growth solidly double digits and puts a floor under VAS expectations in the low to mid 20s.

Worldline (WLN) Q3 revenue was 1% ahead on merchant services timing, but guidance is unchanged and the Street sits at the bottom end of the range. The debate is whether this is a genuine turn in the business.

sector_views.rationale: Tentative renewed buying and rising offense across AI, but investors want steadier prices before adding materially. Choppy trading is the base case.
NXP's in-line print and mixed guide is modestly negative for peers with automotive exposure, though many investors still want to buy IFX after its guide.
SK Hynix expects memory demand to outpace supply through 2030 and HDD supply and demand is tight, though positioning is elevated and good prints are being sold.
KPN and Telenor in line to mixed with flat trading expected, Orange solid with Street estimates needing to rise.

earnings_insights: Adyen Q3: net revenue growth 20% organic (about 200bps inorganic). FY net revenue growth guide of 21-23% y/y constant currency reiterated, implying Q4 acceleration. New FY26 margin expectation about 50% versus Street 52% (consensus estimate), about a 4% FY26 EBITDA downgrade. Medium-term margin guide (above 55% by FY28) withdrawn.

Dassault Systemes Q3 (reported): revenue 2% above consensus. Licences grew 14% versus consensus 2.5%. Recurring revenue organic growth 3% versus consensus 4.2% (miss). Life Sciences grew 1% including some M&A versus consensus -1%. Operating profit about 4% above expectations.

Dassault Systemes FY guidance raised: revenue €6.40-6.46bn (4-5% growth) versus €6.30-6.42bn (3-5%) previously. Consensus €6.37bn excludes the ArisGlobal acquisition. Operating margin guide 32.5-32.7% versus 32.2-32.6%. Q4 Street organic growth 5.6% versus guide of 5-8%.

ASM International Q3 (reported): revenue 5% above consensus, gross profit 6% above. Q4 2026 revenue guide €1.23mn (as printed, likely bn) +/-5% at constant currency, about 3% above consensus at the midpoint. 2027 revenue guide above €5.7bn at constant currency, 5% above consensus and up from the top end of the €3.7-4.6bn range given at the CMD.

Temenos Q3 (reported): revenue $292.8m, 1% below consensus, subscriptions 6% below and maintenance 2% above. EBIT $109.3m, 11% above consensus. Free cash flow missed. FY26 EBIT growth guide raised to about 12% constant currency from about 9% (consensus about 10%). Reported EPS growth guide about 10% from about 7%. ARR growth guide about 12% unchanged.

KPN Q3 (reported): group services revenue 0.4% ahead of consensus, adjusted EBITDAaL 0.9% ahead. FY guidance reiterated. Lost 9k broadband consumers versus -1k last quarter, due to a one-off change in terms and conditions. First 9M FCF flat y/y.

Telenor Q3 (reported): Nordics service revenue 0.6% below consensus, group EBITDA 2% above consensus on opex savings (partly pulled forward from Q4), Nordics EBITDA in line. Working capital +NOK675mn includes a +NOK800mn Grameenphone VAT timing benefit reversing in Q4. FY guide reiterated.
Visa quarter roughly in line (reported) with FY2027 guidance in line with expectations. GS expects VAS expectations to settle in the low to mid 20s growth.

NXP Q3 (reported): broadly in-line results, missed the Street on Industrial, Autos in line. Q4 guidance in line with the Street according to GS but mixed versus bullish buy-side expectations. GS estimates essentially unchanged and about 9% above the Street on 2027 EPS.

Logitech Q2 (reported): revenue in line, gross margin 3.6% ahead of expectations, EBIT 15% ahead. Q3 guide (company, midpoint): revenue $1.36-1.43bn about 6% above consensus, non-GAAP gross margin 41-42% versus 43.5% consensus, operating income $220-255m with EBIT about 1% below consensus. Q3 supplier headwind now $70-80m versus $200m previously expected.
Teradyne Q3 (reported): in line, guidance above on revenue and EPS. EPS beat about 10% versus 20-30% in recent quarters. Q4 revenue guide $1.25-1.35bn versus consensus $1.24bn, flat q/q.

Seagate beat the sell-side consensus on results and guidance. December-quarter guide implies revenue of $4.8bn (about +14% q/q) and operating EPS of $9.20. The source text compares this to a consensus of about $4.57bn, which appears to be the revenue consensus, and gives the stock move as -5% in the summary and -7% in the body.

SK Hynix Q3 (reported): revenue 104tr won (+328% y/y) versus consensus 98tr won, operating profit 88tr won versus consensus 76tr won. Return plan stated as $45bn in the summary and up to $75bn in the body.

Worldline Q3 (reported): revenue 1% ahead. Merchant services organic +4% versus Street 1.6%, helped by delayed churn in Retail that is expected to materialise in Q4 and 2027. Financial Services -3.3% versus Street -6.6% (about -5.1% adjusted). All guidance unchanged.
Logitech FY: Q2 beats with guidance better than feared, and the US after-hours move was larger than the desk expected.
Orange: French convergent ARPU stable to slightly higher q/q and slightly lower y/y, driven by new customer mix. Spain expected to improve further in Q4.
Alphabet and Microsoft report tonight and Amazon reports tomorrow. Samsung reports October 29. SanDisk reports tomorrow with expectations raised after Western Digital.

trade_ideas.rationale: The desk still thinks many investors want to buy IFX after the guide.

risk_factors: Choppy price action after about three months of poor performance may keep investors from adding risk until prices are steadier and more risk events are cleared.
Good prints are being sold (Seagate, Teradyne, Logitech, NXP), showing high buy-side expectations.
Narrow breadth in the Nasdaq bounce, with about 60% of S&P names lower on the day.
Potential significant HDD capacity additions by a smaller competitor overhang Seagate.
Adyen margin reset and withdrawal of its medium-term margin target.
Temenos reliance on large deals since Q2 2025 adds quarterly volatility and the Q4 subscription guide needs 16% growth.
Telenor working capital benefit reverses in Q4 and Bangladesh risks remain.
Dassault ARR has not yet accelerated and the FY guide raise is largely from M&A.
vol_and_positioning: Nasdaq 100 posted back-to-back 1%+ daily gains for the first time in about 3 months while about 60% of S&P names were lower on the day, so breadth is narrow.

Momentum recovered about 2.5% after a roughly 20% drawdown, with GSPRHIMO high-beta momentum up about 8% over three sessions. Global fundamental LS momentum exposure is near YTD lows after the recent de-grossing episode (per GSPB).
Desk flow: floor activity was a 4 on a 1-10 scale with benign flow skews. Asset managers were net buyers of info tech and discretionary and sellers of communication services.

Supply abatement is driving most of the bounce as high-velocity supply and length reduction recede, with emerging but still limited evidence of increased offense across the AI complex after near-zero offense in recent weeks.
Thirty-year hyperscaler bonds led the risk-on move in credit and data centres outperformed in equities.
Buy-side expectations for memory and storage names were further elevated after Western Digital's report, with mixed positioning in HDD names. Seagate sold off about 7% despite a beat (sell-the-news).
Telenor was a relative short heading into results with low expectations.
geopolitical: Telenor flags continuing risk around Bangladesh from inflationary pressure and increased competition, plus potential Bangladesh spectrum payments in Q4.
Orange and Bouygues French telecom consolidation: signing targeted by end-2026, closing by end-2027, long-stop date 6 December, and Bouygues suggested timing could slip a little.

tension_points.bull_case: Topline delivered at 20% organic, the FY revenue guide of 21-23% was reiterated (implying Q4 acceleration), the 2026 cohort is the strongest ever, and the extra investment should add durability to growth.
tension_points.bear_case: Management now expects about 50% margins for 2026 versus Street 52%, a roughly 4% EBITDA downgrade, and withdrew the medium-term margin target of above 55% by FY28.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The FY revenue guide implies Q4 growth accelerates, so a Q4 that fails to accelerate would undercut the topline side of the case.

tension_points.bull_case: Better earnings, oversold conditions and easing selling pressure, with early evidence of increased offense across the AI complex and NDX back-to-back 1%+ gains.
tension_points.bear_case: Narrow breadth, good prints being sold (Seagate -7%, Teradyne -6%), and investors wanting steadier prices before adding materially, so choppy trading is the base case.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Participants are waiting for more stable price action and more risk boxes checked, with Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon results the next events.

tension_points.bull_case: Q3 revenue beat by 2%, licences grew 14%, Life Sciences appears to have stabilised at 1% growth versus consensus -1%, and FY guidance was raised.
tension_points.bear_case: The beat was driven by licences, recurring revenue missed, and the guidance raise largely reflects the ArisGlobal acquisition.
tension_points.what_invalidates: ARR has yet to accelerate, so the desk needs another quarter of evidence of improvement. The next catalyst is the CMD on 17 November.
